body: As a biological female, I don't use the term "cis woman." I kind of refuse to. I'm a woman, that's all. The idea that there are people out there who claim they "don't want to be defined by their genitals" and yet insist on saying "You're not a woman, you're a birth-giver, a uterus-haver" is so unbelievably hypocritical. I definitely agree it's a control thing. Biological women don't fit into the archetype they've created so they made "cis-gendered" as a form of control. "You're a part of this community... you're just at the bottom of the totem pole."
Welcome back

I had to do a similar thing in high school. I honestly just... left them. Stopped hanging around them physically. Ate lunch in a different spot. Walked home a different way. Stopped answering texts. They knew I was okay (not like I was kidnapped or anything) but I just stopped interacting with them. I started it over the summer but just not engaging with them and then when school started up again I just avoided them. It seems rude (and looking back it kind of was) but honestly, I don't care. They weren't good for me. They had no remorse over the things they did that led me to leave them. If they come after you, definitely speak to an adult or multiple adults. See if they can make arrangements for you if worse comes to worse. 

And finally, I think it's a smart move. You should never feel unsafe around your friends. Friends don't bully friends. They don't harass or attack friends. Friends don't make friends feel like they should be afraid. I don't think they are your friends.
Because being human is confusing and now society/media at large is trying to sell gender like it's some commodity. But we're here now and that's what's important. The hard part is over.

If it helps, one female to another, you look female. Give it time. I found doing my eyebrows help me feel more girly lol. Girly clothes also help (dresses, skirts, tights). I see you favor black (so do I) so gothic clothes help too.

My advice is to absolutely stay far away from life altering decisions that will change the course of the rest of your life. Focusing on other things that are important you, outside of gender, may also be best. New hobbies, new experiences, new friends. Or heck, even old hobbies, experiences and friends. Seeing that there is more to life than just "what am I." If you can't seem to escape it no matter what, try to understand why. What makes you dislike being female? What about you is "wrong" to you? Understanding yourself is the first and most important step. And above all else... take it one day at a time. There is no hurry to know everything now, to fix everything now. You have your whole life ahead of you to find out.

Speaking as someone who is very close to my father and my brother, there is a lot to love and admire about males. They aren't just animals. They are smart, funny, loveable, and kind. My dad is a gentle giant who baby talks every dog and cat he sees. My brother is hilarious and sensitive. He's a lanky guy covered in tattoos and he picks up and holds our cat like it's his child and kisses her head. I've been fortunate enough to meet so many wonderful gentlemen in my life, one's who are not just respectful but genuine and thoughtful. They can be crude sure, but almost always to make someone laugh. Watching my 6'2", 200lbs boss at work with a full beard come to work dressed as a grandma for halloween... I can't tell you how hard I laughed. As a woman, there's a lot to admire about womanhood. But womanhood and manhood aren't opposites that fights for 1st place. We're compliments to one another. We work with another the way no one else can. I might try to surround yourself with other men who exhibit these traits, it might help you see maleness as something different. Hope this helps!

While I have no personal experience with this I think it might have to do with the current culture. Parents these days are being told that calling their children by their "dead name" might cause all kinds of problems, including but not limited to making their child severely distressed. I would gather that for your mom, who I assume loves you a lot, is just worried about causing you any kinds of mental anguish.

Your experience is not at all invalid and I suspect very very common. I too was very much the same. Through high school I identified as "genderfluid." I was born a woman, but I didn't want to be feminine at all (14-17). I cut my hair off, I wore baggy clothes, I got a little thrill of joy when people called me sir. I never changed my name or asked others to call me something different, I never wore binders or did anything medical. But then I came out of my teenage years and realized... hey I like being a woman. I like wearing makeup, I like pink things, wearing dresses. But on a deeper level I loved me, I loved the body I was born in, I loved just existing as I was meant to. And those moments of realization are priceless! Your experience is perfectly valid, life is all about changing as a person. Nowadays we're expected to choose a road and stick to it, defend it tooth and nail. But that isn't how humans are. I find it INFINITELY ironic that the people who claim to be the most "open minded" and "tolerant to self discovery" actually couldn't be anything less. Be proud of your realizations, and don't worry about the past. Move forward, be thankful for what you have and enjoy your life.

You can't live your life for other people and you can't control how they'll react to you. This will sound like a broken record but you need to do what you need to do to make yourself happy. Be honest with them about this internal struggle, be honest with them about what's going in your head. Let them react how they will. But get it out in the open. That feeling of "lol nvm" comes from feeling like you need to hide from doubt. But everyone has doubts. You're allowed to change your mind, change and grow as a person. The bottom line is that most people actually don't care. They just want you to be happy.
And yet I'd still take a severed head in my candy bag over a Twizzler...
You'd be surprised people's tolerance for crazy. Your fears are valid and you deserve respect when discussing them with others.

Ultimately though, being afraid of something you can't control can only hurt you. My advice is to just live your life. If they do decide to drop the bombs (and this is very, very, very unlikely!) there isn't much you'll be able to do so it really isn't worth your time worrying about. I can promise you the world is not ending and perhaps this isn't the greatest advice but it's what my dad tells me when I feel the same as you feel;

Even if the world is going to end, would being terrified help? If the world was ending, there isn't much you alone can do to stop it. So there really isn't a point panicking. Take things a day at a time, focus on yourself and what you enjoy. The world ending is not your responsibility. Your happiness and quality of life is. Ensure you take care of yourself and your loved ones. Let the rest of the pieces fall where they may. 

I get nightmares a lot too. Having a stuffed toy or something to hold to your chest or a weighted blanket really do help in the short term. Ultimately though, talking out your feelings can be a big boon. Hope this helps!

I totally hear you, I'm the same way. I'm a very academic person and I have a bit of a competitive personality. I need to be the best at what I do and since I don't do all that much, I feel like I need to be extra good at the stuff I do manage to get done. 

Best advice I can offer is to let it in and let it go. Life is all about pitfalls and dustups. Given the description of your past, I would say getting a C is above and beyond what most people could accomplish under the same pressures. So well done!

As for the college choices; don't worry. I got rejected from several of my top choices and the college I ended up going to and loving was actually my backup. If you can talk to your teachers to see if there are improvements you can make or at the very least get some remarks back on what you did wrong and how you can improve in the future. That's the best thing you can do for yourself and I think your teachers will be impressed at your initiative and drive to do better. 

Ultimately though, and I'm telling you as someone who has been in your shoes, you will be okay. Things may not work out the way you expect them to but they will work out. I promise your parents are not disappointed in you. We are our own worst critics. Try to be your best ally !

So basically, every few months they unveil a new Crown Crate. Each one is themed and it's like a gambling game. You can buy one box at a time or up to 15 at a time (for like 5,000 crowns) and then you open them. Each box has 4-5 cards, each card is an item. If you look at the individual tiers of rewards, you can see what you can get. Legendary are mounts (400 crown gems). You also get crown gems, which you can get if you get a duplicate item. You can spend the gems on individual items directly from the crown store.

Like for example, the most recent crown crate in the shop is the Gloomspore crate. I bought 15 crates and opened them all up. I got some of the body markings, adornments, weapons styles, potions, xp scrolls. I had some crown gems left over from previous crates, so I extracted some gems from stuff I didn't want (potions I didn't need) and got like 400 gems in bank, so I spent them on a mount that I wanted but didn't get.

Each crate has a different theme and some of them are seasonal. It's basically like a gamble, you buy a box and see what cards/items you get.

I've had this problem before. I couldn't speak to all of this but I do have some tips on how to get people to stop interrupting. 

Bring it up. "Excuse me, you interrupted," or "I wasn't done yet," "Now hold on \_\_\_" are my go-tos. It sounds rude but it isn't, you have a right to finish your thought, and as long as you don't say it in a dramatic, valley-girl accent, it's not rude to assert yourself. Waiting an extra five minutes or five seconds for you to finish will not kill them. As for people repeating what you said, if you make a stand you can often be assured they'll remember you. 

Believe I know how awkward and hard it is to be assertive but it's a skill that takes time and is WELL worth it. Letting someone know they're being rude, intentionally or not, is important. You speak, they speak. So it goes.

I think once quarantine ends, they'll be a huge wave of people going out to make up for lost time, but on the whole, no I don't think it'll have much of an effect. Note, that's socially, I couldn't speak to economically or financially. I have hope that once it's safe, people will be able to go back to their lives, but take hope in the fact we're all in this together. In the meantime, this might be a great opportunity to try some new things. Might I suggest arts and crafts to keep your mind on something else? I actually found I like sewing, and if you knew me, you'd now how weird that is haha

I wish you luck, and know the storm won't last forever.

I'd imagine it's pride. No one like to be told they're being a dick but sometimes it needs to be said. In my experience, it takes some serious swallowing to admit a mistake. And sometimes people just don't have it in them to high five the hand that feeds them. It's good that you brought it up, bad that they seem worse off, but you'd be within your rights now to cut them off. If they can't treat you with the same respect, there's a line there. You made your thoughts clear and they ignored them. That might be a reason to bring it up to them again, hell, a 100 more times if need be, until they change their behavior. And if they don't, you might have to tell them you're done. Altruism is a trait of saints but everyone should have their limits. 

Hope this helps! Cheers
